messages.text: What is non-signaling tester, and which product-related measurement decisions depend on understanding it?

The knowledge base did not validate a final answer, so the evidence is insufficient for a fully supported recommendation. It did return partially supported notes:

A **non-signaling tester** is an RF measurement tester used without establishing full protocol signaling with the device under test. In the returned evidence, the clear example is **R&S CMP180** running **RF measurements in non-signaling mode** for production, where avoiding signaling saves test time.

Product-related measurement decisions that depend on understanding “non-signaling” include:

| Decision | Why it matters |
|---|---|
| **CMX500 vs CMP180 for Wi‑Fi 7** | CMX500 is positioned for R&D signaling / interworking testing; CMP180 is positioned for production non-signaling RF testing. |
| **Signaling vs non-signaling test mode** | R&D may require signaling behavior and real-world TX/RX interaction; production RF test often prioritizes speed and repeatability using non-signaling mode. |
| **Whether CMP180 is the right production RF tester** | CMP180 is described as a production/R&D non-signaling tester, especially for WLAN production RF measurements. |
| **Which CMP180 WLAN options are needed** | Non-signaling WLAN measurements may drive options such as IEEE 802.11be SISO, true MIMO 2x2/4x4, true MIMO 5x5/6x6, and WLAN PER acknowledgment measurements. |
| **Which CMP180 cellular RF options are needed** | Non-signaling cellular RF testing may require NR FR1 single-carrier, multi-carrier, MIMO, LTE, or LTE C‑V2X measurement options. |
| **MIMO scale decisions** | CMP180 configuration depends on whether 2x2, 4x4, or larger WLAN/MIMO setups are required. |
| **Whether 480 MHz WLAN waveform support is a requirement** | The evidence mentions CMP180 loopback validation of a 480 MHz WLAN waveform as a possible Wi‑Fi 8 / IEEE 802.11bn candidate, not a formal Wi‑Fi 8 requirement. |
| **CMP200 for mmWave / FR2 non-signaling RF** | CMP200 with remote radio heads is positioned for 5G NR FR2 non-signaling RF parametric testing in R&D and high-volume manufacturing. |
| **Whether CMX500 can cover non-signaling R&D use cases** | The notes indicate CMX500 Callbox also has non-signaling verification / GPRF generator use cases, so “signaling vs non-signaling” is not only a product-name distinction. |

In short: understanding “non-signaling tester” mainly prevents mixing up **protocol/application signaling test decisions**—often associated with CMX500—with **fast RF production measurement decisions**, often associated with CMP180 or CMP200.

data.answer:
已查到可引用的部分資料：

A non-signaling tester is characterized here as an RF measurement tester, separate from signaling-protocol testing, and the explicit production example is R&S CMP180 running RF measurements in non-signaling mode to save time [32][3].  
| Product-related measurement decision | What depends on understanding “non-signaling tester” | Supported facts |
|---|---|---|
| Choosing CMX500 vs CMP180 for Wi‑Fi 7 | Use CMX500 for R&D signaling / interworking testing, and use CMP180 for production non-signaling RF testing [2]. | CMX500 covers Wi‑Fi 7 R&D signaling and interworking testing, while CMP180 covers production non-signaling RF testing [2]. |
| Choosing signaling mode vs non-signaling mode | Wi‑Fi 7 R&D testing needs signaling mode and real-world RF TX/RX measurements, while WLAN production RF measurements are performed in non-signaling mode to save time [1][3]. | CMX500 is the multi-technology multi-channel signaling tester for R&D scenarios [1]. |
| Choosing CMP180 for production RF | CMP180 is positioned as the production / R&D non-signaling tester and is optimized for WLAN production non-signaling RF measurements [4][3]. | CMP180 supports Wi‑Fi 6E, Wi‑Fi 7, and 5G NR FR1 up to 8 GHz with bandwidths up to 500 MHz [3]. |
| Choosing WLAN measurement options on CMP180 | Non-signaling WLAN production measurements can require options such as WLAN IEEE 802.11be SISO measurements R&S CMP-KM352, WLAN true MIMO 2x2 and 4x4 measurements R&S CMP-KM360, and WLAN true MIMO 5x5 and 6x6 measurements R&S CMP-KM361 [66]. | CMP180 also lists WLAN packet error rate acknowledgement measurements R&S CMP-KM365 [66]. |
| Choosing cellular RF measurement options on CMP180 | Non-signaling cellular RF measurements can require NR FR1 measurements such as R&S CMP-KM600 single carrier, R&S CMP-KM602 multi-carrier, and R&S CMP-KM604 MIMO [66][67]. | CMP180 also lists LTE measurements R&S CMP-KM500 and LTE C‑V2X measurements R&S CMP-KM570 [66]. |
| Choosing MIMO scale on CMP180 | One CMP180 can support 2x2 MIMO testing, and two CMP180 instruments can be combined for 4x4 MIMO access-point testing [3]. | CMP180 integrates two analyzers, two generators, and two sets of eight RF ports [3]. |
| Choosing whether a 480 MHz WLAN waveform is a product requirement | CMP180 demonstrates loopback validation of a 480 MHz WLAN waveform, but the source calls it only a potential Wi‑Fi 8 / IEEE 802.11bn candidate, not a formal Wi‑Fi 8 specification [3]. | The source does not provide the waveform format, sample rate, modulation, EVM, uncertainty, or required option details for that demo [6]. |
| Choosing CMP200 for mmWave / FR2 non-signaling RF | CMP200 with CMPHEAD30 or CMPHEAD50 forms a 5G NR FR2 nonsignaling one-box test solution for RF parametric testing in R&D and high-volume manufacturing [46]. | CMP200 targets pure radiated mmWave setups for assembled devices and mixed radiated/conducted setups for mmWave RF ICs [46]. |
| Choosing whether CMX500 can cover a non-signaling R&D workflow | CMX500 Callbox use cases include non-signaling verification [16]. | CMX500 GPRF Generator is a CMX500 non-signaling use case for ARB, CW, dual tone, and replay `.wv` waveform generation [19]. |
【推論】Understanding “non-signaling tester” mainly prevents mixing protocol/application signaling decisions for CMX500 with RF production measurement decisions for CMP180 and CMP200 [2][3][46].
